To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The experimental TL glow curves from felspar can be described by the same continuous distribution of activation energies; (2) The TL glow curves can also be described by a physical kinetic model of localized recombination in a random distribution of donor-acceptor centers; and (3) The same kinetic parameters (b ∼ 1.7 and the activation energy) are obtained from the empirical general order analysis and from the physical model.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of TL signals from feldspar, which are important in luminescence geochronology.
the development of a physical model for thermoluminescence in feldspars.
the analysis of the experimental TL glow curves using both empirical and physical models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both the initial rise method and the model proposed by Pagonis and Kitis (2003) can provide a good description of the kinetic behavior of TL in plagioclase, but the physical significance of the kinetic parameters obtained using the two approaches is not the same.

both the empirical approach and the physical model are able to provide a good description of the experimental data, but that neither approach can be used to provide a detailed understanding of the underlying luminescent process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TL signal from plagioclase has a complex structure, with at least two different components, and the TL signal from a single sample can be characterized by two different kinetic models.
the experimental TL glow curve can be described accurately using both a continuous distribution of activation energies, or a continuous distribution of recombination centers.

, although the physical model of TL glow curve analysis based on localized electronic recombination is able to provide a better fit to the experimental data, it is not able to provide a unique solution for the kinetic parameters of the underlying luminescent system.
